articles_hidden.title: The Two Accountings of Gendered Violence: Criminal Order, Police Legitimacy, and Recorded Violence in Chicago
articles_hidden.authors: Igor Novaes Lins
articles_hidden.abstract: Women are a rising share of the people shot in Chicago, and the police series that should register violence against them moves with the structure of the city's criminal order. The paper follows both patterns across 77 community areas, 2010 to 2024, separating what armed territorial order does to violence from what it does to its record. The female share of shooting victims rises from about one in ten in the early 2010s to about one in six after 2022, and Cook County vital records, which never pass through a police station, reproduce the trend. The gender composition of victims is equivalent across gang identities within three percentage points, so what varies is volume. Where more gangs compete over the same ground, registered civilian-initiated violence rises by seven to nine percent per standard deviation of fragmentation, in domestic and non-domestic series alike, a movement at the institutional gateway. Under concentrated control, violence against women changes place. Their share of gunfire moves downward in every specification, with conventional confirmation in only one, while the male series stays flat. The domestic share of their homicides rises with concentration in every window, so consolidation pulls women out of the street's line of fire and leaves the violence against them at home, where the registered series shows no movement. The record of violence against women, these results imply, measures access to the state as much as harm, and the harm side requires a second, non-police accounting that the paper specifies as a concrete program.

articles_hidden.title: Caregiver-centred networks and the sustainability of later-life care: A conceptual framework
articles_hidden.authors: Ruizhe Liu; Brian Khumalo
articles_hidden.abstract: Informal caregiving is central to later-life health, yet research has focused primarily on older adults themselves or on caregivers’ individual stress experiences. Less attention has been paid to the structural and relational conditions that shape how caregiving responsibilities are distributed and sustained over time. Building on the Stress Process Model, this paper develops a caregiver-centred framework that integrates four analytically dimensions of network: received support, perceived support, network diversity, and substitute availability. We conceptualize these dimensions as interrelated components of a dynamic feedback system linking caregiver-centred network properties, caregiver burden, and recipient health outcomes. A central contribution is the formalization of substitute availability, defined as the functional capacity of other actors to assume caregiving responsibilities when the primary caregiver is unavailable or overburdened. The framework also identifies contextual conditions, including gender norms, kinship obligations, and demographic change, that shape how caregiving networks are organized. We discuss how this framework can be operationalized through ego-centred and whole-network methods, and outline implications for public health interventions and future longitudinal research.

articles_hidden.title: Produção científica de um programa de educação ambiental no licenciamento federal: Análise bibliométrica do PEA-Pescarte
articles_hidden.authors: Vitor de Moraes Peixoto
articles_hidden.abstract:
O licenciamento ambiental federal obriga as operadoras de petróleo a financiar programas de educação ambiental, executados por universidades públicas ao longo de mais de uma década. Avalia-se o efeito socioambiental desses programas; não se mede o conhecimento que eles deixam. Este artigo faz esse levantamento para o PEA-Pescarte por revisão sistemática PRISMA 2020, que reúne acervo
institucional, auditoria de planilha e busca em três bases: 356 obras em 382 registros de 284 autores, descritas por cinco redes. A colaboração se organiza pelo pertencimento ao programa, não pelo organograma de pesquisa, e se concentra num articulador. A citação interna só se torna visível na leitura dos textos completos. O corpus, as redes e o protocolo ficam públicos em https://pescarte-acervo-7402cb.gitlab.io, produto deste artigo. Este artigo é resultado de pesquisa financiada pelo Projeto de Educação Ambiental (PEA) Pescarte que é uma medida de mitigação exigida pelo Licenciamento Ambiental Federal, conduzido pelo IBAMA.

articles_hidden.title: The LINGACON Multilingualism Assessment Standard (L-MAS): Definitions, Thresholds, and a Review of Survey Practice
articles_hidden.authors: Areg Hovhannisyan
articles_hidden.abstract: How many languages does a person speak? This question—fundamental to understanding human linguistic capacity, global connectivity, and the effectiveness of language education policy—has no standardized measurement protocol. In the course of constructing the first global estimate of Average Language a Person Speaks (ALPS) across 235 countries and territories (a companion study currently in preparation; Hovhannisyan, forthcoming), we discovered that existing data sources use at least six distinct and mutually incompatible methods for assessing multilingualism. These methods produce dramatically different results: For a single country (Zambia), the same survey program (Afrobarometer, n.d.) yielded ALPS estimates of both 2.72 (Round 4) and 5.92 (Round 10), depending on how the question was asked. Meanwhile, entire regions—the Arab states, Latin America, and most of Asia—appear to have no publicly available, standardized multilingualism survey data. We present a taxonomy of current measurement approaches, document their biases and incompatibilities, identify three previously undescribed sources of systematic error (the diaspora residual, the linguistic concealment effect, and the dubbing–subtitling asymmetry), and propose a comprehensive solution: the LINGACON Multilingualism Assessment Standard (L-MAS), a five-level measurement framework scalable from a single survey question (Level 1, zero cost) to a comprehensive national audit with tested proficiency (Level 4) to a longitudinal tracker enabling measurement of multilingualism change over time (Level 5). If Level 1 were adopted by the five major cross-national survey programs, approximately 118 countries—covering over 85% of the world’s population—would have comparable multilingualism data within a single survey cycle. The full L-MAS specification is freely available at l-mas.com.

articles_hidden.title: Bucks for Bumps: How Paid Parental Leave Pays Off for Firms
articles_hidden.authors: Hillary Cookler
articles_hidden.abstract: Firms use benefits such as paid parental leave (PPL) to attract and retain employees. In the U.S., which lacks broad public PPL benefits, firms increasingly provide this benefit. Systematic evidence of its benefits remains limited, due in part to the absence of comprehensive data on firm policies. Using a novel, hand-collected database of firm policy changes, this paper estimates the causal effect of PPL expansion on employee retention using a differences-in-differences approach. PPL expansions reduce departure rates by 3.1%, an effect equivalent to a permanent wage increase of 1.8%. Retention gains for women are concentrated among the lowest paid and those in the most junior roles, while retention gains for men are broad-based. At the firm level, retention gains concentrate in the interior of the internal labor market flexibility distribution and among firms with moderate firm-specific human capital, and they are robust to concurrent benefit changes and to firm revenue trajectories. Public PPL programs, by contrast, show no comparable retention effect, consistent with the non-portability of firm-provided benefits. Combining fertility estimates from the American Community Survey (ACS) with worker and firm data, the paper calculates the expected costs of PPL provision and compares them to retention gains: at realistic utilization rates, PPL expansions generate positive net returns to firms.

articles_hidden.title: Evaluation of Initial Mental Health Impacts of Federal Changes in Identity Document Guidance on Transgender and Nonbinary Persons
articles_hidden.authors: Clair Kronk; Devin Madden; Rishabh Jain; Ashley Michelle Morales; Diddier Prada; Hill Wolfe; Carol R. Horowitz
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background: To assess potential mental health impacts of restrictions on gender marker changes by transgender and nonbinary people in the wake of Executive Order (EO) 14168. 
Methods: From March to July 2025, we surveyed transgender and nonbinary persons from a large northeastern medical system regarding gender markers on documents, current mental health status, and perspectives on current sociopolitical climate. 
Results: Quantitative analyses (n = 368) revealed identification as Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish and exploring one’s gender identity were related to greater distress. Gender marker change status on passports was associated with serious psychological distress, though this relationship was not statistically significant among other document types. Qualitative responses highlighted extensive concerns over mental wellbeing, political targeting, and staying in the U.S., while also showcasing perceived protective factors, and concluding with acknowledgement of transgender rights as human rights. 
Conclusions: Our findings describe a high rate of distress and pervasive fears tied to EO 14168 and the broader political environment.

articles_hidden.title: The Bank-Financed Margin of Trade Credit: Evidence from Italian Innovative and Ordinary SMEs
articles_hidden.authors: Angelo Leogrande; Mauro Di Molfetta; Valeria Nortarnicola; Maria Giovanna Trotta; Antonio Volpe Plantamura
articles_hidden.abstract:
Design/methodology/approach. The sample comprises 63,858 firm-year observations on 9,983 Italian innovative start-ups, innovative SMEs and ordinary SMEs between 2015 and 2024, drawn from statutory accounts. The collection period is regressed on bank debt with firm and year effects under nine estimators and six alternative scalings of both sides of the equation. A cluster analysis comparing six algorithms across eleven validity indices partitions the firms by financial configuration, and the equation is re-estimated within each group. Six regression learners fitted to the same demeaned data test the linearity and additivity restrictions the panel imposes.
Purpose. Trade credit and bank credit have been described as substitutes for three decades, yet a competing tradition finds them complementary, and the evidence has not converged. This paper argues that the disagreement is definitional rather than empirical. Almost every study measures trade credit received, treating the firm as a borrower choosing between two funding sources, while the credit the firm extends to its own customers enters as a control or not at all. The paper estimates both margins on one sample and asks whether bank borrowing lengthens or shortens the credit small and medium enterprises grant.
Findings. Bank indebtedness and the collection period move together within firms, at 0.48 days per percentage point of bank debt over turnover and positive under every estimator, while the same equation on payables returns −0.43. A model of a supplier facing a bank credit limit generates both signs from one first-order condition and bounds pass-through between zero and one, which the data satisfy at 0.126 euro per euro. The association reaches 0.81 among long-cycle firms, halves where liquidity is abundant, and declines from 0.80 to 0.50 across the decade as bank credit loosens.
Originality/value. The paper reconciles two literatures previously read as contradictory by estimating both margins of trade credit on one sample and deriving both signs from a single decision problem. It identifies a measurement problem the field has not addressed: because trade credit granted and bank debt are conventionally scaled by turnover, the estimated coefficient ranges from +0.48 to −0.12 across ratio specifications, so published estimates are not mutually comparable. It is also the first study of trade credit supply in the certified Italian populations of innovative start-ups and SMEs.

articles_hidden.title: I'm Dreaming of a Green Christmas:  Observational Loyalty Card Data Reveal the Health and Environmental Impacts of Festive Food Purchasing
articles_hidden.authors: Emma Wilkins; Alice Rose Kininmonth; Piyush Mohan; Mark Alan Green; Mark S Gilthorpe; Victoria Jenneson; Alexandra Johnstone; Michelle Morris
articles_hidden.abstract:
Background: The festive season is associated with weight gain that often persists into the new year, but the specific purchasing behaviours driving this are not well quantified. Christmas is also thought to be a period of disproportionate environmental impact, though the contribution from food purchasing has not been explored. The objective of this study was to use retail transaction data from a major UK supermarket to examine seasonal patterns in purchases of less healthy food and drink products (High in Fat, Sugar and/or Salt, HFSS), and the greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) from sales, and to quantify the extent to which purchasing behaviours during the festive period differ from the rest of the year.
Methods: Daily food and non-alcoholic beverage transaction data for 2022 for loyalty card holders living in Yorkshire and Humber were obtained from a major UK retailer. Products (>27,000) were classified as HFSS or non-HFSS using the UK Nutrient Profile Model and linked to GHGE estimates per kg. Changes in HFSS sales and GHGE were examined between the festive period (1-31 December 2022) and the baseline period (1 Jan-30 Nov 2022) using four metrics, expressed as the daily average over the two periods: HFSS sales (kg), percentage of all sales by weight that were HFSS (%HFSS), total GHGE from sales (kg-CO2-eq) and GHGE per kg (kg-CO2-eq·kg-1). 
Results: Marked increases in total HFSS sales and GHGE from sales were observed in the festive period (+25% and +15.3% respectively). The additional festive GHGE footprint was equivalent to 3,000 return flights from London to the North Pole. Consumers purchased proportionally more HFSS foods (+10.1%) and more foods with higher GHGE per kg (+6.6%). These changes were driven by shifts towards products that were both less healthy and more environmentally costly, particularly beef, chocolate and lamb.
Conclusion: Christmas is traditionally associated with generosity, celebration and plentiful food. Our study shows that this festive cheer comes at a cost to health and the environment. With a little more thought about what food we buy, the festive period can still be enjoyed while also benefiting population and planetary health.

articles_hidden.title: Female recreational runners’ perspectives of running-related injury risk and management: A qualitative exploration
articles_hidden.authors: Emily Authurs; Vivienne Chuter; Kim Hébert-Losier; Benjamin Peterson
articles_hidden.abstract:
Introduction: Recreational running enhances both mental and physical health. However, the high incidence of running related injury (RRI) is a key barrier to participation. Previous research has attempted to establish the risk factors for RRI, with the most well-established being previous injury and training errors. However, previous reductionist approaches for mitigating RRI risk factors have been largely unsuccessful, with interventions primarily focusing on isolated factors and not considering runners’ perceptions and experiences. 

Methods: We used an interpretive phenomenological analysis framework, qualitative data collection via focus groups, and reflexive thematic analysis to develop an understanding of the perceptions and experiences of female recreational runners in relation to RRI. Eleven female recreational runners were recruited across three focus groups to investigate participants’ perspectives and experiences relating to RRI risk, prevention, management, and health seeking behaviours. Each focus group was analysed using a six-phase reflexive thematic analysis approach to identify underlying themes. 

Results: Five interconnected themes (‘The Run’, ‘The Runner’, ‘The Injury’, ‘The Networks’, and ‘The Gear’) were identified as having an influence on whether a runner can remain injury-free, and the management of RRI. Analysis of runners’ perspectives and experiences cumulated in the development of the Perceptual RRI Risk, Prevention, and Management Nexus model. 

Conclusion: The female recreational runners interviewed particularly relied on informed self-regulation with guidance of past advice and previous experiences to manage RRI and identify RRI risk. The runners perceived modifiable and non-modifiable RRI risk factors should be considered when developing future injury prevention programs for runners like them.

articles_hidden.title: SOBRE LOS REGÍMENES POLÍTICOS EN EL MUNDO Y SU EVOLUCIÓN (1900-2025)
articles_hidden.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles_hidden.abstract: Este ensayo analiza la evolución histórica de los regímenes políticos mundiales desde 1900 hasta 2025 empleando las bases de datos del proyecto Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem). Revisa los fundamentos teóricos de la democracia y la autocracia, destacando que la tercera ola de autocratización contemporánea no opera mediante golpes de Estado tradicionales, sino a través de una erosión interna y sutil de los contrapesos institucionales. Mediante índices como el de regímenes en el mundo y el de democracia electoral, la investigación examina la distribución bimodal global, las disparidades regionales y la correlación entre elecciones competitivas y garantías liberales, concluyendo que la preservación de la libertad requiere instituciones sólidas y una actuación institucional temprana.

articles_hidden.title: Why Play When AI Can Win: The Non-Transferability of Participation and the Visibility of Dignity
articles_hidden.authors: Kengo Tomita
articles_hidden.abstract: Knowledge work is learning to hand itself over. Drafting, analysis, computation, and even the role of a practice opponent can now be delegated to artificial intelligence, often with better and faster results. This paper asks what does not move in that handover. Drawing on Bernard Suits's analysis of games, I distinguish an achieved state from participation in the activity that produces it and defend an agent-relative non-transferability theorem: another agent may realise the goal state on my behalf, but cannot thereby make it true that I pursued that goal under constitutive constraints I accepted as reasons. AI can deliver the state of affairs; it cannot deliver the fact of participation. The theorem is independent of whether machines can achieve, play, or matter morally. It leaves a human question: under what cultural conditions can people continue activities they know machines can perform better? I use an explicitly extended Kantian contrast between price and dignity to propose that AI, by supplying functionally equivalent outputs at scale, makes newly visible the non-equivalent fact of participation. Japanese professional shogi, which publicly encountered machine superiority and continued, is examined as a completed historical case in which recognition for serious play persisted after technology made its instrumental outputs substitutable. The case illustrates a condition analysis centred on dignity apparatuses: cultural forms that prevent appraisal by comparative performance from exhausting recognition of participants' standing.

articles_hidden.title: Policy Failure in Hong Kong's Waste Charging Scheme: A Bourdieusian, Critical Discourse, and Content Analysis
articles_hidden.authors: Alan
articles_hidden.abstract: This paper advances a field-theoretic framework for understanding policy implementation failure in hyper-dense, post-colonial cities when quantity-based waste charging is layered onto unreformed socio-spatial and institutional fields. Drawing on policy failure scholarship (McConnell, 2010a, 2010b; Bovens & 't Hart, 1996; Matland, 1995) and Bourdieu's practice theory, it demonstrates that Hong Kong's suspended Municipal Solid Waste Charging Scheme failed not from rejection of the polluter-pays principle, but from structural misalignment between a thin pricing instrument and the durable habitus of convenience disposal, ambiguous enforcement authority, and weak state symbolic capital. Three contributions follow. First, the field-restructuring precondition hypothesis: economic instruments in dense vertical cities require prior reconfiguration of infrastructure, institutional positions, and bodily hexis before pricing can function. Second, through comparison with Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and European PAYT schemes, Hong Kong's failure reflects an accelerated, compressed version of implementation challenges visible elsewhere when field transformation is elided. Third, preparatory measures—GREEN@Community infrastructure and Green$ incentives—generated unintended cultural and symbolic capital around recycling, creating a partial habitus shift despite the scheme's suspension, complicating linear narratives of policy failure. Environmental governance in dense Asian cities must be reconceptualised as long-term field restructuring rather than rapid behavioural levering.

articles_hidden.title: Imagining transformative pathways towards peaceful and equitable futures in the Korean peninsula
articles_hidden.authors: HyeJin Kim; Vitnia Lee; Hyeonjeong Kim; Miyoung Yeo; Yeoungjun Yeo; Youngcheol Cho; Gwanwoo Jin; Justin Johnson; Bohun Kang; Dirk N. Karger
articles_hidden.abstract: The Korean Peninsula faces the intertwined challenges of a polycrisis: an unresolved war and rapid development followed by demographic contraction, inequality, accelerating biodiversity loss, and intensifying climate risk. Achieving nature- and people-positive futures in this context requires finding alternative pathways: levers and actors of change, and their sequences and scaling. Citizens constructed transformative pathways from present-day Korea to four Korean Nature Futures visions. A methodology combined the Nature Futures Framework, Imagination Infrastructure, and Seeds of Good Anthropocene with narratives refined through the multi-level perspective and social-ecological systems theory. The four 2025-2050 pathways trace changes through five phases: present-day challenges, seeds of change, breaking points and shocks, and the emergence and stabilisation of new systems by 2050. Comparative analysis across ten domains – social, technological, ecological, economic, political, cultural, military, religious, identity, and the DMZ – identifies shared strategies and pathway-specific mechanisms. Across pathways, the DMZ is reimagined from a line of division into an anchor of ecological peace, with human and non-human actors recognised as agents of transformation. The study offers a transferable methodology for transformative scenario development in contested geopolitical settings and a proof of concept for anticipatory governance toward equitable and peaceful futures ‘Living in Harmony with Nature’.

articles_hidden.title: Tracking AI’s Scientific Anatomy: A Novel Framework for Analyzing the Use and Diffusion of AI in Science
articles_hidden.authors: Liangping Ding; Cornelia Lawson; Philip Shapira
articles_hidden.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) promises to transform science by accelerating knowledge discovery, automating processes, and introducing new paradigms for research.  However, there remains a limited understanding of how AI is being utilized in scientific research. In this paper, we develop a framework based on GPT-4 and SciBERT to identify AI’s role in scientific papers, differentiating between Foundational, Adaptation, Tool and Discussion modes of AI research. This allows us to capture AI’s diverse contributions, from theoretical advances to practical applications and critical analysis. We examine AI’s trajectory across these modes by analyzing time series, field-specific, and country trends. This approach expands on search-term based identification of AI contributions and offers insights into how AI is being deployed in science.

articles_hidden.title: A Fork in the Road for Global AI Governance: To Repair or Reconfigure Expert-Led Governance?
articles_hidden.authors: Adam McCarthy; Olajide Olugbade
articles_hidden.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a live object of global governance, with expert-led institutional arrangements emerging across an international regime complex. While scholarship on epistemic communities and science-policy interfaces treats expertise as a mechanism for coordination under uncertainty, recent work in Objectual International Relations (O-IR) and Science and Technology Studies foregrounds knowledge politics, contested authority, and the co-productive character of governance. We bring these perspectives into conversation with AI governance through a reflexive workshop design using Nominal Group Technique, drawing on two expert workshops in the UK and US.
Findings show that expert panels remain valued for structuring debate, coordinating knowledge, and lending legitimacy to policy action. Yet participants identified tensions around exclusion, elite and private capture, weak accountability, geopolitical constraints, and temporal misalignment between institutional processes and technological change. An object-centered analysis further shows that AI remains an unstable governance object; the knowledge required to govern it is contested and unevenly distributed; and expertise itself is politically charged and institutionally unsettled. We synthesize these tensions into two pathways: Repair and Reconfiguration. Repair seeks to stabilize AI as a governable object, standardize relevant knowledge, and secure expert authority through institutional continuity and procedural refinement. Reconfiguration seeks to keep AI contested, broaden credible forms of knowledge, and reshape expertise through participation, reflexivity, and engagement with politics. The framework provides a critical lens for assessing emerging institutional designs for global AI governance and the trade-offs they entail.

articles_hidden.title: Different histories, similar discrimination: Field experimental evidence of discrimination against Black parents in the Dutch childcare market
articles_hidden.authors: Stefanie L. Sprong; Valentina Di Stasio; Bram Lancee; Eva Zschirnt
articles_hidden.abstract: While a vast body of research documents discrimination against ethnoracial minorities, including Black people, existing studies rarely consider how the diverse historical relationships of different Black groups may shape patterns of discrimination. Using data from the first field experiment in the Dutch childcare sector (N = 1,354), we examine discrimination against ascribed Black parents enquiring about childcare spots in the Netherlands. Rather than aggregating all ascribed Black parents into a single category, we compare ascribed Black parents with names associated with former Dutch colonies to those with names associated with Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), expecting the former group to face less discrimination. We find robust evidence that ascribed Black parents face discrimination in access to childcare: compared to ascribed White majority parents, they are significantly less likely to receive a spot offer, and their enquiries are more likely to be ignored altogether. SSA ascribed Black parents are also more likely to experience neglectful treatment in written correspondence. Otherwise, levels of discrimination do not significantly differ between former-colonies and SSA ascribed Black parents, suggesting discrimination against Black parents more generally.

articles_hidden.title: Dynamics of Self-Employment Following Motherhood: A Comparison Between Korea and the United States
articles_hidden.authors: Wonjeong Jeong
articles_hidden.abstract: Parenthood increases the need to adjust paid work, especially for mothers, who continue to shoulder a disproportionate share of carework. This makes it important to understand not only whether mothers remain employed after childbirth, but also how they reorganize work across the life course. This paper examines self-employment as one potential way mothers incorporate flexibility into their post-birth careers. Adopting a life course perspective, I compare new mothers in South Korea and the United States and trace their employment arrangements from first birth to ten years afterward. Using descriptive analysis, sequence analysis, and multinomial logistic regression, I assess whether self-employment emerges as a distinct pathway in mothers’ careers and how its role differs across institutional contexts. The results first show that self-employment is more common in mothers’ careers than cross-sectional estimates would suggest in both countries. However, the way it is incorporated differs substantially. In Korea, self-employment more often follows spells of non-work and is more likely to be full-time, suggesting that it can operate as part of a return to paid work strategy when rse-entry into wage employment is difficult. In the United States, self-employment is more often part-time and embedded within continued attachment to wage employment. Multinomial logistic regression provides only limited support for the idea that self-employment trajectories primarily function as a flexibility strategy, as they are only weakly associated with women’s educational resources and are not clearly associated with second birth. Overall, the findings show that self-employment is part of many mothers’ post-birth careers, but not a general flexibility strategy; its meaning is shaped by institutional context.

articles_hidden.title: Burden Without Backlash? Trust and Procedural Fairness in Response to Welfare Compliance Demands
articles_hidden.authors: Aske Halling; Frederik Godt Hansen
articles_hidden.abstract: To access public services, citizens often navigate complex administrative requirements. These demands are introduced to ensure program integrity and maintain public support for welfare policies, yet they may create barriers for those in need. While prior studies on policy feedback and administrative burden show that burdensome encounters can reduce trust among welfare recipients, less is known about how the general public reacts to compliance demands. Stringent requirements may signal that programs are protected against fraud, potentially increasing perceptions of fairness and trust among non-recipients. We further hypothesize that compliance demands have positive effects on these outcomes when: 1) individuals are non-recipients rather than recipients of welfare services, and 2) the welfare recipient is perceived as undeserving. To test these hypotheses, we conducted a pre-registered vignette survey experiment in Denmark with a sample of the general public (N = 1,624) and welfare recipients (N = 409). We find that stringent compliance demands increase perceptions of fairness but do not affect trust in government among the general public. We find no support for the moderation hypotheses. Our findings challenge prevailing understandings of administrative burden, showing that stricter requirements can enhance perceived fairness without undermining trust—regardless of welfare experience and deservingness perceptions.

articles_hidden.title: Sustainable Urban River Space Transformations: An Interdisciplinary Spatial Agenda for Research and Practice
articles_hidden.authors: Claudiu Forgaci; Francesco Nattino; Angelica Stan; Fakhereh Alidoost; Mila Avellar Montezuma; Bilge Nur Bektaş; Lieke de Boer; Daniele Cannatella; Rodrigo d'Avila; Ilse Ellenbroek
articles_hidden.abstract: Riverfront regeneration increasingly features in current sustainable urban transformations worldwide. However, this phenomenon is not yet grasped in its full complexity, which challenges our understanding of what constitutes a sustainable transformation. In this paper, we argue that adopting a morphological approach that treats rivers and cities equally is essential for understanding urban river spaces and their transformations. Drawing on 17 worldwide cases of river space transformation, we identify recurring challenges and opportunities, including climate adaptation, land-use change, data availability, context sensitivity, and knowledge transfer. We inventory current methods, datasets, and tools to assess their suitability and sufficiency for answering current research questions and enabling new ones. We also posit that integrated and scalable approaches are needed to combine qualitative and quantitative methods, support cross-case comparison, and remain adaptable to local conditions. As a first foundational step towards local integrated and global cross-case analyses, we introduce urban river space delineation as the basis for comparable analysis and present rcrisp, an open-source tool for automated and scalable morphological delineation of urban river spaces. Finally, we emphasise that advancing this agenda requires community and capacity building across disciplines and sectors, so that methods and tools can be shared, refined and extended. By connecting cases, methods and communities, the paper calls for collective action to build a common language and evidence base for sustainable urban river space transformation.

articles_hidden.title: Impacto de la prescripción social sobre la soledad en adultos mayores: una revisión rápida de la literatura
articles_hidden.authors: Silvia Juliana Navas Barba; Maria Alejandra Ospino Vasquez; María Sofía Pardo Gaitán; María José Patarroyo Villalobos; Angie Xilena Quiroga Cortés; Francisco Palencia-Sánchez
articles_hidden.abstract:
Introducción: El envejecimiento poblacional incrementa la vulnerabilidad a trastornos de salud mental, exacerbados por la presencia de comorbilidades. En este contexto, la soledad emerge como un factor de riesgo determinante para el deterioro cognitivo, la enfermedad cardiovascular y la mortalidad. La prescripción social, un modelo que vincula a pacientes de atención primaria con recursos comunitarios no clínicos, se perfila como un posible abordaje terapéutico. El objetivo de este estudio fue sintetizar la evidencia científica más reciente sobre el impacto de estas intervenciones en la soledad de los adultos mayores.

Metodología: Se realizó una revisión rápida de la literatura bajo los lineamientos de Cochrane Rapid Reviews y PRISMA 2021. Se buscó en PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science y literatura gris (Google Scholar, IRIS) entre 2021 y junio de 2026. Se incluyeron estudios en adultos mayores (≥60 años) que evaluaran la prescripción social frente a atención habitual o nula, con la soledad como desenlace. Se excluyeron protocolos, poblaciones hospitalarias y modelos basados exclusivamente en tecnologías digitales sin interacción humana.

Resultados: De 498 registros identificados, se incluyeron cuatro estudios (2024–2026): un metaanálisis de 26 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados, una revisión de alcance y dos estudios cuasiexperimentales. El metaanálisis evidenció una reducción significativa de la soledad (SMD=0,59; IC95%: 0,47–0,71), destacando el efecto de las intervenciones artísticas. Un estudio cuasiexperimental mostró menor probabilidad de incremento de soledad mediante grupos comunitarios durante la pandemia; en contraste, el otro no halló una reducción significativa de la soledad, aunque sí mejoras en depresión y apoyo social.

Discusión: La prescripción social muestra un efecto favorable sobre la soledad, especialmente mediante actividades artísticas y significativas. No obstante, la persistente heterogeneidad metodológica, conceptual y contextual limita la generalización de los hallazgos hacia entornos latinoamericanos.

Conclusiones: Pese a la heterogeneidad, la prescripción social es una herramienta con potencial para mitigar la soledad en la vejez. Existe una clara oportunidad en Colombia para desarrollar y evaluar modelos adaptados localmente, articulados con la atención primaria para construir vínculos sociales duraderos.

articles_hidden.title: Diagnosing a Correlation Paradox: How Loose Derivation Chains Conceal Theoretical Anomalies in Criminological Research
articles_hidden.authors: Jonathan R. Brauer
articles_hidden.abstract: Criminological research programs frequently report statistically significant findings while obscuring systematic patterns that should drive theoretical development. Paul Meehl’s concept of logical derivation chains, or the sequence of logical steps linking theoretical propositions to empirical predictions, provides a diagnostic framework for understanding why empirical tests so often fail to produce cumulative theoretical progress. While recent work has identified criminology’s “precision crisis” abstractly (Brauer & Day, 2025), this paper operationalizes derivation chain analysis as a practical diagnostic method. Using Gottfredson and Hirschi’s (1990) self-control theory as a strategic case study—chosen because its derivation chain is unusually well-documented, making structural problems harder to attribute to researcher oversight—I demonstrate how auxiliary assumptions accumulate to create compound derivation chain failures that render empirical tests uninterpretable. Analysis of the Grasmick et al. (1993) scale reveals a “correlation paradox”: a statistically significant correlation (r = -.31, p < .0001), typically celebrated as strong support, masks theoretical failure for nearly 40% of individual cases. Item-specific analysis across cross-cultural samples from Lviv, Ukraine and Dhaka, Bangladesh reveals substantial heterogeneity and failure of measurement invariance within supposedly unidimensional scales, while cognitive and behavioral measures disagree in classifying individuals in approximately 40% of cases. These systematic anomalies, or high self-control individuals who engage in crime and low self-control individuals who refrain, represent precisely the phenomena that should drive theoretical development, yet correlation-based analytic standards render them invisible. To demonstrate that derivation chain problems extend beyond personality constructs, the framework is also briefly applied to swift-certain-fair deterrence programs (Project HOPE), revealing parallel auxiliary accumulation in policy evaluation research. The paper provides a derivation chain self-assessment checklist and four constraint-aware research practices (individual-level prediction assessment; item-specific analysis; systematic anomaly documentation; auxiliary assumption mapping) as practical tools for building more theoretically progressive criminological science.

articles_hidden.title: After CAHOOTS: Service decline, shifting police attention, and a rising arrest rate
articles_hidden.authors: Nathan Burton; Mathilde Lafay; Leo Uhlig; Alex Gollier; Jennifer Linnaea; Chris Medina; Rori Rohlfs
articles_hidden.abstract: For more than three decades, CAHOOTS dispatched unarmed teams of medics and crisis workers to certain 911 calls in Eugene, Oregon. On April 7, 2025, the program ceased operations in Eugene, though it continues in neighboring Springfield. This report provides a quantitative analysis of 911 calls and responses in the aftermath of the closure, attempting to account for the roughly 235 calls per week that CAHOOTS had been handling. We find that police now spend substantially more time on CAHOOTS-type call categories, even though the Eugene Police Department (EPD) has absorbed only a minority of CAHOOTS’ former call volume. More than half of the former demand no longer appears in any city record available to us, and the calls that do still receive a response end in arrest roughly twice as often.

articles_hidden.title: La cláusula que nadie escribió: el deber de información del promitente vendedor profesional, la buena fe del artículo 1546 y el desistimiento que no lo fue (comentario a la sentencia de la Corte Suprema de 10 de agosto de 2026, rol N° 34.305-2025)
articles_hidden.authors: Andrés Gabriel Varas Quijón
articles_hidden.abstract:
La Primera Sala de la Corte Suprema, en sentencia de 10 de agosto de 2026 (rol N° 34.305-
2025), acogió la casación en la forma deducida por una promitente compradora, anuló la sentencia de la
Corte de Apelaciones de Santiago y, en la de reemplazo, confirmó la resolución de una promesa de
compraventa inmobiliaria por incumplimiento de la sociedad promitente vendedora, con las restituciones
mutuas y la cláusula penal pactada. El interés del fallo está en su fundamento: la integración del contrato por
la buena fe objetiva del artículo 1546 del Código Civil. Las condiciones suspensivas pactadas —
regularización del terreno, rol de avalúo, plano aprobado e inscrito, factibilidades de luz y agua— dependían
de la promitente vendedora; siendo ésta una sociedad inmobiliaria, «como se advierte de su razón social»,
era la llamada a informar a su contraparte la época de su cumplimiento, «pese a no constar en una cláusula
determinada». Y la compradora que, ante esa nula información, comunica que no prorrogará el plazo no se
desiste inmotivadamente: exterioriza una decisión conforme a lo pactado. El comentario reconstruye el
caso, sitúa la decisión en la dogmática de la buena fe integradora y de los deberes de información del
contratante profesional —con la mirada puesta en el artículo 1112-1 del Code civil y en la Ley N° 19.496—,
examina el desistimiento que no lo fue a la luz del artículo 1552, la obligación de citar a notaría como
incumplimiento autónomo, la vía de la casación en la forma con sentencia de reemplazo, y cierra con una
guía de redacción de promesas inmobiliarias y un decálogo del promitente prudente. La tesis: la cláusula que
nadie escribió estaba escrita desde 1855 — el artículo 1546 la redactó por todos.

articles_hidden.title: Formal and Informal Institutions Interactively Increase Judicial Independence: Evidence from Israel and Cross-National Data
articles_hidden.authors: Andrew O'Donohue
articles_hidden.abstract: Comparative research emphasizes that independent judiciaries act as bulwarks against democratic backsliding. Yet we know less about why judicial independence is more resilient in some cases than others. Whereas existing scholarship often contrasts the effects of formal versus informal institutions, this paper emphasizes how their interaction fosters judicial independence. I theorize that one understudied institution—a super-majority requirement for selecting high court judges—increases judicial independence. Moreover, this formal institution better protects judicial independence when complemented by an informal institution—a practice of appointing groups of ideologically distinct judges that I call the Noah’s Ark strategy. I test this institutional theory using cross-national and within-country evidence. Leveraging original data on judicial selection institutions in 139 countries, I find super-majority requirements are significantly associated with increased judicial independence. To show how formal and informal institutions interact, I conduct a case study of the country with the world’s highest super-majority requirement, Israel. Using quantitative data on 16,000 Israeli Supreme Court decisions and qualitative interviews with high-ranking judges and politicians, I show that formal and informal institutions constrained the government’s judicial appointments—but that the government’s undermining of informal institutions weakened judicial independence. These findings illuminate how the interaction of formal and informal institutions fosters judicial independence and democratic resilience.

articles_hidden.title: The Rise of Competitive Authoritarianism in Israel: The Paradox of Uneven and Contested Competitive Authoritarianism
articles_hidden.authors: Oded Haklai; Andrew O'Donohue
articles_hidden.abstract: Scholars and democracy indices disagree over whether prominent cases of autocratization have crossed the threshold into competitive authoritarianism. One reason for these disagreements, we argue, is that there are varieties of competitive authoritarianism. We theorize that competitive authoritarian regimes vary in the degree to which they are uneven, repressive, and contested. We then evaluate empirically whether Israel meets Levitsky and Way’s definition of competitive authoritarianism. We find that by Levitsky and Way’s criteria, Israel crossed the line into competitive authoritarianism under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. But competitive authoritarianism is not a one-size-fits-all category. We show that Israel’s competitive authoritarian regime is uneven, in that autocratization is more severe in some areas than others; less repressive than many autocracies; and contested, in that opposition parties remain competitive, even when they are structurally disadvantaged. This unevenness and contestedness have led to Israel’s misclassification thus far.

articles_hidden.title: Book Review Multimodality and Time: A Social Semiotic Approach (preprint)
articles_hidden.authors: Henrika Florén
articles_hidden.abstract: This review examines Theo van Leeuwen's Multimodality and Time: A Social Semiotic Approach (2025), which foregrounds the role of timing and rhythm in meaning-making. The book develops a Social Semiotic approach for analysing time-based multimodal texts and performances, including music, film, language, and everyday interactions. Distinguishing between time, timing, social timing, and time-based texts, van Leeuwen argues that timing is socially constructed and that rhythmic structuring is central to how meaning unfolds across modes. The review considers the book's treatment of rhythm, temporality, and multimodal analysis, and discusses the ways in which it extends existing multimodal approaches by bringing temporality to the forefront of analysis. The review concludes that the book makes a significant contribution to Multimodal Social Semiotics and visual communication research and offers valuable directions for future research.

articles_hidden.title: Who cares? The gendered nature of mobility of care in São Paulo
articles_hidden.authors: Joana Barros; Agnes Silva de Araujo
articles_hidden.abstract: Quantitative evidence on mobility of care remains scarce and geographically uneven because conventional surveys classify trips by destination and purpose, obscuring caring responsibilities within the evidence used for transport planning. This study expands evidence from the Global South by examining the prevalence, characteristics and gendered distribution of mobility of care in the São Paulo Metropolitan Region. Carrying-passenger trips from the 2023 Origin–Destination Survey are used as a partial proxy for mobility of care and combined with trip-purpose information to distinguish caring activities. Descriptive and negative binomial analyses examine differences by gender, age, race and socioeconomic stratum and interactions between gender and these characteristics, including household car ownership. Carrying passengers accounted for 15.6% of adult trips and displayed distinctive patterns of purpose, mode and trip frequency. Women recorded higher rates than men, particularly for school- and home-related trips, whereas men’s carrying was relatively more work-related. Gender gaps differed in magnitude by race and in both magnitude and direction across the life course. Rather than following a progressive socioeconomic gradient, gender disparities formed a nonlinear U-shape, narrowing to apparent parity in the middle strata but widening asymmetrically at both ends. Car ownership further differentiated gender gaps by socioeconomic stratum and trip purpose. Methodologically, the findings support carrying-passenger data as a useful, although incomplete, means of making care visible in conventional travel surveys. Conceptually, they challenge uniform and gender-neutral accounts of everyday mobility, demonstrating that inequalities in mobility of care emerge through intersections between social positions, caring purposes and household transport resources.

articles_hidden.title: Closed for the holidays: why the annual cycle of protest is institutional, not thermal
articles_hidden.authors: Syed Mustafa Quadri
articles_hidden.abstract: Protest is not spread evenly through the year, and the standard explanation is climatic: people take to the streets when the weather permits. Using 984,026 ACLED demonstration events across 159 countries and 28 years, merged with ERA5 temperature climatology, we show that the annual cycle is institutional rather than thermal. Each hemisphere reaches its annual minimum during its own local summer, in opposite calendar months, a pattern that survives every leave-one-year-out test in both hemispheres. That minimum is not heat. For 66 countries we code school holidays from their published start and end dates and derive month indicators by a fixed rule, so which break counts as the long one is decided by its duration rather than by our expectations about its temperature. Breaks suppress protest by 17.6 percent when they fall in a country's hottest months, 8.7 degrees Celsius above its own annual mean, by 15.8 percent when they fall in its coldest, 8.9 degrees below, and by 11.8 percent when they carry no thermal contrast whatever, 0.1 degrees. In the twelve countries whose annual temperature range averages 2.7 degrees, where there is almost no thermal cycle for a calendar to be confused with, breaks still cut protest by 13.9 percent. Rotating each country's calendar by a random number of months destroys the effect in all 200 draws. Temperature does carry an independent association, which we report rather than dismiss: per comparable unit it is about a third the size of the break effect, and its sign is negative, so warmer months see less protest, not more. The break effect is roughly twice as large in richer and more open countries as in poorer and more closed ones, although income and democracy cannot be separated from one another. A composition check supports the mechanism: student identified protest, whose institutional calendar is documented and unambiguous, is two and a half times more seasonal than protest in general and shows the two term shape. We also report a negative result that bears on how such work should be done. The northern annual peak is February and is stable across all 27 year-drops and all 10 country-drops, but the southern peak is not identifiable: it moves between March, May, October and November depending on the window chosen, because six countries carry 91 percent of the southern temperate sample and a single episode, the Chilean uprising of October 2019, shifts the annual peak by seven months. A five-year window yields an apparently stable southern peak that a 28-year window does not support. The annual rhythm of protest tracks institutions in session; claims about hemispheric peak alignment do not currently have the data to stand on.

articles_hidden.title: Time Discounting, Relative Risk Aversion, and Educational Inequalities
articles_hidden.authors: Herman Gerbert van de Werfhorst
articles_hidden.abstract: Using recently collected survey data merged with register data from the Netherlands, this study examines the predictive value of personal concerns with avoiding downward mobility and time discounting preferences for later school careers. Following implications of relative risk aversion theory and time discounting theory, the results show that children from low-income households need to have both a concern to avoid downward mobility and a higher willingness to wait for longer-term returns in order to make it to the higher tracks. Starting from the premise that, given earlier performance, it would be rational to go on to the highest possible track to avoid downward mobility, the Dutch early-tracking system assumes that students oversee a long educational future to optimize their educational investment. This assumption is less valid for low-income students, which could explain why early tracking increases socioeconomic inequalities in school careers.

articles_hidden.title: Changes in homeownership and entry into parenthood in the Nordic countries
articles_hidden.authors: INVEST Flagship; Jessica Nisén; Lars Dommermuth; Peter Fallesen; Sofi Ohlsson-Wijk1
articles_hidden.abstract: Since 2010, fertility levels have declined unexpectedly in all Nordic countries, with record lows being reached in recent years. The reasons for these declines are unclear, except that fewer people are becoming parents. The aim of this study was to investigate whether changes in housing tenure played a role in the declined entry into parenthood. We expected that changes in housing tenure, particularly a decline in homeownership related to housing affordability challenges among young adults, may have contributed to this decline. Using harmonized Nordic individual-level register data, we assessed to what extent changes in housing tenure, changes in fertility behavior within tenure groups, or both, contributed to the decline. Discrete-time event history models and multivariate decomposition were applied. According to our results, homeownership among young adults declined in the 2010s in Denmark and Finland – but not in Sweden or Norway. The decline in first births was only partially attributable to compositional change in housing tenure along with other socioeconomic factors in Denmark, Finland and Sweden. Entry into parenthood declined among women, regardless of their tenure status, in all four countries during the 2010s, suggesting the importance of behavioral changes. However, the decline was more pronounced among renters than homeowners.

articles_hidden.title: Specification, Heterogeneity and Functional Form in the Determinants of Small-Firm Profitability
articles_hidden.authors: Angelo Leogrande; Mauro Di Molfetta; Valeria Nortarnicola; Maria Giovanna Trotta; Antonio Volpe Plantamura
articles_hidden.abstract: Studies of small-firm profitability estimate financial structure as the focal regressor and treat cost composition as an unexamined control. This paper reverses the emphasis and places both blocks in one equation, estimated on 91,756 firm-year observations covering 14,913 unlisted Italian firms across three regulatory regimes. Three methods interrogate different assumptions on the same sample: panel estimation across fourteen specifications, unsupervised partitioning selected on eleven validity criteria, and machine-learning regression applied to the same firm-demeaned data. The capitalisation coefficient is not identified. It moves from +0.177 under two-way fixed effects to between −0.12 and −0.28 under five instrument sets, all of which fail because profitability persists at 0.271, so any lagged financial ratio embeds past profit. The labour-share coefficient is stable across estimators, groups and functional forms, and the paper tests whether that stability is arithmetic, since return on assets and the labour share are consecutive lines of one statement. It is not: value added over total assets varies by a factor of 2.8 across the four operating archetypes recovered from the data, while the coefficient varies by 1.07. The accounting identity explains part of the magnitude and none of the stability.

articles_hidden.title: Documentation Gap Analysis: Independent Audit of TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan
articles_hidden.authors: Paul Rekaris
articles_hidden.abstract:
This independent audit evaluates the TGA COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Monitoring Plan (February 2021). The Plan operationalised National Cabinet's commitment to enhanced pharmacovigilance accompanying provisional approval, covering 68.4 million doses, 91.2% of Australia's rollout. Enhanced monitoring claims cannot be independently verified when the underlying processes are undocumented. This audit tests whether that verification is possible.

The audit finds a systematic failure to demonstrate the enhanced monitoring underpinning Australia's largest provisional medicine rollout. Only 3 of 19 audited outputs (16%) are fully documented; 16 (84%) are partially or not documented. This is despite the TGA's own OAIC-directed searches surfacing 2,218+ pages of potentially relevant material in September 2024, none identified as Plan-implementation documentation. The TGA reports 148 signals investigated and 57 regulatory actions taken (the signal count was updated to 150 in the subsequent Question on Notice 559). No audit trail links signals to actions, and 91 signals have no documented disposition in the record. The OAIC found that the implementation records "cannot be found or do not exist".

Senior TGA officials told the Senate (9 October 2025) that monitoring occurred through "day-to-day processes," without systematic tracking against Plan objectives. The TGA cannot demonstrate documented implementation of its own Safety Monitoring Plan. This is a potential failure of regulatory accountability for the largest provisional medicine rollout in Australia's history.

The audit's open-source methodology applies ISO 19011:2018, ANAO guidance, and OSINT principles to public and FOI records, providing evidence for independent investigation and pharmacovigilance reform aligned with international standards and recognised good practice, including ICH E2E and CIOMS. It is published under CC BY 4.0: open access and independently replicable.

The audit repository, containing the supporting evidence, primary sources, methodology, version history, and replication resources, is maintained at: https://github.com/paulrekaris/TGA-COVID19-Vaccine-Safety-Monitoring-Audit

Updated versions of this paper are available on SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6333058

Version 6 note: This revision adds substantial documentary and regulatory analysis, including a new Appendix mapping the national enhanced-monitoring commitment, February 2021 Plan, provisional-registration framework, sponsor obligations and Commonwealth accountability requirements. It also updates FOI/OAIC, Senate and TGA evidence and refines regulatory framing, assessment scope and implementation-tracking analysis. Audit ratings and overall conclusions are unchanged.

articles_hidden.title: Context-Dependent Resource Conversion: Estimands and Decompositions in the Capability-Ecological Dynamic Model
articles_hidden.authors: Subir Hait
articles_hidden.abstract: Social-science models often summarize the association or effect of a resource with one coefficient or average treatment effect, even when the return to that resource varies across actors, relationships, institutions, and time. This article develops the Capability-Ecological Dynamic Model (CEDM), an estimand-centered middle-range framework for context-dependent resource conversion. Building on capability theory, capital and social-capital theory, stratification, multilevel sociology, heterogeneous-effect methodology, experimental development economics, and transportability, CEDM distinguishes resource possession from access, mobilization, and realized conversion into functionings. It defines an observed conversion surface and the local conversion return, then formalizes conversion modification, ecological shaping, cross-capital complementarity or substitution, conversion instability, context comparison, and dynamic path dependence. Formal results establish aggregate masking; an exact symmetric conversion-structure/composition decomposition; a multilevel decomposition of conversion-return variance; a pseudometric for comparing conversion-return functions; and the logical independence of substantive conversion stability from inferential robustness. Social capital is treated as role-dependent: network structure, accessible resources, mobilized resources, and realized conversion are distinct objects, and social capital may be a focal resource, a modifier of another resource's return, or a contextual property depending on the estimand. Causal interpretation is separated from descriptive conversion and requires a defensible intervention and identification strategy. A reproducible multilevel simulation with 150 contexts and 40 actors per context illustrates the framework: the seeded sample has a pooled mean conversion return of 0.0105, 61.6% of realized conversion-return variance lies between contexts, and 80.3% of that between-context component is associated with ecological support in the specified linear projection. CEDM does not replace established theories or estimators; its proposed contribution is a common estimand-centered language for studying when, where, and through which social conditions resources acquire heterogeneous returns.

articles_hidden.title: Captured by the Ballot: Non-Partisan Judicial Elections and Democratic Erosion in Mexico
articles_hidden.authors: Brett Ryan Bessen
articles_hidden.abstract: Public tolerance for democratic erosion is often attributed to voter partisanship. Voters are thought to overlook undemocratic maneuvers to support the partisan in-group. Yet, backsliders  often disavow traditional parties and frame their reforms as non-partisan. I examine the role of voter partisanship in non-partisan elections, showing how elite manipulation of the information environment can generate partisan outcomes that facilitate backsliding—even when citizens prefer non-partisan outcomes on average. I examine Mexico’s 2025 judicial elections, pairing a conjoint experiment with an analysis of the electoral results. While the conjoint indicates that voters preferred independent judges, the electoral results indicate that government-aligned candidates on illicitly circulated voter guides (acordeones) received the most support, contributing to the partisan capture of the Supreme Court. Elite manipulation of the information environment and electoral incentives—rather than partisan preferences among the eligible electorate—were primary contributors to the court’s partisan capture.

articles_hidden.title: Cross-Asset Shock Diffusion: A Reproducible Test of Residual Underreaction, Shock Coherence, and Trading Economics
articles_hidden.authors: Alina Khaybullina
articles_hidden.abstract:
This paper examines whether differences in the speed with which traded assets respond to a common market shock can predict subsequent relative returns. The public framework combines a lagged rolling factor model with Absorption Gap (AG), which measures an asset’s response error, and Shock Coherence (SC), which characterizes the market state on that date.

The study evaluates the signal using executable next-open timing, explicit transaction costs, dependence-aware inference, randomized-signal benchmarks, chronological diagnostics, alternative normalizations, portfolio sensitivity analysis, and machine-learning extensions.

The sample contains 24 ETFs from 4 January 2010 through 28 August 2026, with eight factor proxies excluded from the 16-asset traded cross-section. The paper connects an economic hypothesis about heterogeneous information absorption to an executable quantitative trading framework and provides a reproducible research design for testing cross-sectional predictability, market-state conditioning, and implementation economics.

The contribution is both empirical and methodological: it develops a transparent framework for measuring relative shock absorption, separates cross-sectional signal information from market-state effects, and emphasizes timing integrity, transaction costs, robustness, falsification, and reproducibility in quantitative strategy research.

articles_hidden.title: Rethinking Socialism in the Era of Human Genomics
articles_hidden.authors: Jorge Antonio Benitez
articles_hidden.abstract: This article examines twentieth-century socialist regimes as large-scale social experiments in the light of new insights from the sequencing of human genomes. It contends that extreme collectivization, while driven by ideological, political, and economic factors, may also have partially underestimated patterns of human behavior shaped by evolutionary and gene-environment dynamics. Historical cases show that institutional models lessening property rights and sense of agency required coercion and subsequent reform. Based on findings from genome-wide studies and behavioral genetics, this paper emphasizes that human social traits are polygenic, probabilistic, and context-dependent, yet not infinitely malleable. It views behavioral patterns as statistical distributions driven by gene-cultural dynamics placing political extremism as a key factor in institutional long-term stability. In this framework, extreme privatization and extreme collectivization can be considered equally wrongful.

articles_hidden.title: ESG Implementation in Small and Medium Cosmetics Industries: Certifications, Barriers, and Theoretical Implications in the Brazilian Context
articles_hidden.authors: Orlando Nastri Neto; Murilo Dotti Garcia
articles_hidden.abstract: The world's fourth-largest cosmetics industry operates largely through small and medium-sized enterprises. In Brazil, these SMEs account for the largest share of sectoral production and are also the least prepared to meet the growing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) demands that increasingly condition access to international markets, supply chains, and capital. This article examines that mismatch. Drawing on an integrative literature review, we combine Legitimacy Theory (Suchman, 1995), Stakeholder Theory (Freeman, 1984), and the Resource-Based View (Barney, 1991) to analyze how certifications such as Ecocert/COSMOS, Leaping Bunny, B Corp, SA8000, GRI, and EcoVadis function as instruments of legitimation, and why most Brazilian cosmetics SMEs fail to obtain them. We identify six interdependent barrier dimensions and propose the concept of “ESG legitimation capacity” as a theoretical proposition for future empirical research. The main contribution is showing that the problem is not a lack of ESG awareness, but a structural resource gap that no single voluntary compliance instrument can solve on its own.

articles_hidden.title: Legacy admissions preferences and underrepresented minority enrollment at highly selective US institutions
articles_hidden.authors: Orr Teva; Kai LaMothe; Joyce Li; David Wang; Régan Schwartz; Chad M. Topaz
articles_hidden.abstract: Legacy preference in undergraduate admissions is a policy favoring applicants with family ties to alumni. Critics argue that it reproduces advantage across generations. A basic question remains: Do institutions that publicly report considering legacy enroll different shares of underrepresented racial and ethnic minority (URM) students? No centralized dataset has linked comparable admissions-priority reports to enrollment composition. In Common Data Set reports, institutions rate admissions criteria on a shared scale and disclose enrollment by race and ethnicity. We assemble these reports into a panel of highly selective US institutions covering 2010–2022 and verify the enrollment data against federal records. Institutions that report considering legacy status enroll first-year URM shares 6 to 8 percentage points lower than institutions that do not, net of sector and other reported priorities. Because every private institution in the sample reports considering legacy, the estimate is identified by the contrast among public institutions that do and do not consider legacy status. The association is statistically significant in the primary specification and remains negative across controls, functional forms, and covariates including selectivity and size. Parallel associations appear for Asian enrollment share and Pell Grant receipt. In an expanded sample with enrollment from federal records, the URM association is smaller and imprecise, while the combined URM and Asian association remains large and statistically significant. Samples are modest and unobserved characteristics remain uncontrolled, so we interpret these patterns as descriptive associations, not causal effects. The issue has taken on heightened importance after Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard.

articles_hidden.title: A Party for People Like Me. Voter-Party Linkages and Dynamic Group Identities.
articles_hidden.authors: Tarik Abou-Chadi; Markus Kollberg; Francesco Raffaelli
articles_hidden.abstract: We introduce a theory of dynamic identity-based linkages between parties and voters. Social groups are associated with political parties. When people identify with a group and that groups is seen as associated with a political party, they become more likely to view a party as a party for people like me, which should increase party support. As salient identities can vary over time, these linkages are dynamic and can change party support. We test this framework using a three-wave panel survey experiment in the UK. Increasing the salience of working-class (wave 2) and rural identities (wave 3) makes people more likely to regard the party most associated with these groups (Labour and the Green Party) as a party for people like me. It also increases party support. We contribute a framework for party-voter linkages that goes beyond programmatic competition and provide a micro-foundation for the growing literature on group appeals.

articles_hidden.title: Toward a Computational Account of Perception and Choice in Situational Action Theory
articles_hidden.authors: Chae Rose
articles_hidden.abstract: Situational Action Theory (SAT) explains action through a perception–choice process, yet key components of this process remain verbally specified. This paper develops a proof-of-concept computational formalisation of SAT, selectively drawing on active inference to represent how personal morality and perceived moral context shape perceived action alternatives and how deterrence and self-control subsequently influence choice. A computational demonstration shows how moral correspondence, moral conflict, and the conditional relevance of controls can be represented continuously without imposing discrete decision states. The formulation provides a framework for translating SAT’s verbally specified process propositions into explicit computational hypotheses that can be systematically examined and empirically tested.

articles_hidden.title: Rethinking Sovereignty through Planetary Thinking: Europe, the Technosphere, and Ecological Redirection
articles_hidden.authors: Elodie René; José Halloy; Alexandre Monnin
articles_hidden.abstract: This article rethinks European sovereignty under planetary conditions. Rather than treating sovereignty as independence or strategic autonomy, it conceptualizes it as a relational capacity to govern vulnerabilities and interdependencies within the Technosphere. Bringing political theory and international relations into dialogue with Earth system science and ecological redirection, we show how energy, critical materials, digital and scientific infrastructures bind European agency to planetary-scale technical systems. We develop three claims. First, sovereignty must incorporate planetary temporalities and the material reproducibility of technical systems, illustrated through the distinction between living and zombie technologies. Second, the EU’s technological catch-up strategy vis-à-vis the United States and China risks reproducing dependencies and unsustainable trajectories. Third, ecological redirection offers a sovereign practice centered on organized exits, structural sufficiency, care for negative commons, and democratic inquiry into attachments and dependencies. On this basis, multilateralism is recast not as a constraint on sovereignty but as an infrastructure for governing interdependence, negotiating vulnerabilities, preserving scientific continuity, and organizing just technological transitions. The chapter thus proposes a planetary conception of European sovereignty as a dynamic, democratic capacity to compose material viability, political legitimacy, and international cooperation over time.

articles_hidden.title: Bioethical guidelines of sexual-attraction change in psychotherapy
articles_hidden.authors: Joseph Nicolosi
articles_hidden.abstract: This article reexamines ethical and scientific objections to psychotherapeutic interventions that alter clients’ unwanted sexual attractions. While major mental-health organizations label such interventions as controversial, ineffective, and ethically problematic, recent studies demonstrate that some interventions can lead to changes in individuals’ sexual attractions. These interventions significantly differ from the therapies criticized by these organizations. This article examines these criticisms and responds to them, identifies neuroscientific mechanisms that appear to be responsible for sexual attraction changes, and proposes a framework for ethically implementing evidence-based, client-led interventions that influence sexual attraction.

articles_hidden.title: DE LA MAREA ROSA A SOMOS MÉXICO: EL ESFUERZO PARA CREAR UN PARTIDO
articles_hidden.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles_hidden.abstract: El texto analiza el surgimiento de la organización política Somos México (derivada de la Marea Rosa y opositora a la autodenominada Cuarta Transformación). Examina el contexto histórico de las reformas electorales impulsadas por Andrés Manuel López Obrador (Planes A, B y C) y el proceso de obtención de su registro como partido político nacional ante el INE en 2026, enfrentando impugnaciones jurídicas y observaciones sobre su denominación y emblema.

articles_hidden.title: Administrative Coordination Cost Theory and a Citizen-Centred Model of Integrated Public Service Delivery
articles_hidden.authors: 김동욱
articles_hidden.abstract:
This study develops a citizen-centred model of integrated public service delivery grounded in Administrative Coordination Cost Theory (ACCT). ACCT focuses on coordination work generated when citizens cross organisational and institutional boundaries, including locating the competent agency, repeating information, resubmitting documents, confirming case transfers, tracking status, and recovering from incomplete referrals. It conceptualises these tasks as costs whose responsibility is distributed between citizens and public organisations.

Using a theory-building and institutional-design approach, the study draws on administrative burden, transaction-cost theory, collaborative governance, one-stop service research, whole-of-government coordination, government and research-institute reports, and relevant Korean statutes in force as of 30 August 2026. It defines five central constructs: boundary density, externalisation of coordination responsibility, citizen-borne administrative coordination costs, internalisation of coordination responsibility, and total coordination costs. Eight testable propositions and an operational framework link the generation of coordination tasks, the allocation of responsibility, and service outcomes.

The proposed model follows the citizen’s service pathway from initial contact and lawful information verification to accountable transfer, confirmation of intake, professional decision-making, service commencement, status tracking, follow-up, correction, and appeal or review. Specialised legal authority remains with competent organisations, while cross-boundary coordination responsibility is translated into observable administrative actions. Data and artificial intelligence support guidance, classification, duplicate-check reduction, and status management, while legally authorised human decision-makers retain final responsibility for decisions affecting rights, benefits, or sanctions.

The model is applied to eleven policy areas in Korea, including social-security administration, welfare organisation, vouchers, delivery systems, smart welfare and finance, early-childhood education and care, school-age care, youth, adults, older people, and disability services. It proposes concrete institutional alternatives, including a Social Security Integrated Executive Agency and a standalone Ministry of Welfare model, as policy applications for comparative testing rather than as organisational forms logically required by ACCT. The study’s main contribution is to treat the generation and allocation of cross-boundary coordination work as an independent object of analysis and to connect it with service access, continuity, dropout, equity, rights protection, and public-sector operating costs.

articles_hidden.title: El impuesto invisible: La lógica del Neomercantilismo Burocrático en el comercio global.
articles_hidden.authors: Federico Estrada
articles_hidden.abstract: Este artículo introduce y formaliza el concepto de "Neomercantilismo Burocrático" para explicar la insistencia en la exclusión comercial en economías contemporáneas que mantienen aranceles nominales bajos. El problema central se ubica en la dualidad estatal donde, bajo una fachada de apertura internacional, el Estado implementa una estructura administrativa asfixiante que protege a las empresas dominantes frente a la destrucción creativa. A través de un diseño de investigación mixto, el paper propone de forma preliminar el Índice de Neomercantilismo Burocrático (INB) para cuantificar la brecha entre la apertura nominal y el cierre practico, complementado con un modelo econométrico de panel para evaluar la reasignación deficiente de capital desde la innovación hacia el Lobbying. Los resultados preliminares demuestran que, ante un incremento en las trabas burocráticas, la inversión en I+D de las empresas protegidas disminuye en favor de la protección normativa, validando inicialmente la tesis de la pereza corporativa. Se concluye que el Neomercantilismo Burocrático representa un retroceso cualitativo en la integración global, sugiriendo que el desarrollo interno no requiere únicamente liberalización arancelaria, sino la destrucción integral de la estructura burocrática excesiva que captura el dinamismo competitivo de los mercados.

articles_hidden.title: Private Government Behind the Gates: Homeowners’ Associations, Institutional Lock-In, and the Democratic Commons
articles_hidden.authors: George Skouras
articles_hidden.abstract:
Common-interest developments house tens of millions of Americans and increasingly assign homeowners’ associations functions once performed by municipalities. This Article examines physically gated communities as a particularly visible subset of that broader system. It argues that mandatory private residential governance can provide valued services while also creating problems of accountability, amendment, public access, and regional coordination. The Article combines doctrinal analysis, institutional theory, and descriptive housing data; because no national dataset precisely enumerates gated communities, its population estimates are presented as 
The Article also presents a stylized voting model showing how amendment provisions measured against all eligible owners can create institutional lock-in when participation is low. The model is illustrative rather than predictive: its central result follows from the interaction among the denominator, the approval threshold, turnout, and support among participating owners. The Article then evaluates state and local reforms, including judicial threshold-reduction procedures, quorum-sensitive voting rules, transparency protections, and prospective infrastructure conditions.
